text:
nina: Quick question — for the payment-migration we want to send selected debug traces to Sentry (dev + staging only). Is it OK to include a hashed email and customer_tier in the event tags? Hashing with sha256. Is that still PII? cc @liam @sarah
liam: Short answer: hashed identifiers can still be considered pseudonymous data under our policy. Need a documented purpose, TTL, and to ensure no reversible mapping is kept.
sarah: Agree with @liam. Per Data Classification we treat user identifiers as at least 'sensitive'. If the hash is irreversible and there's no mapping stored it's lower risk, but you still need to: 1) justify purpose, 2) set a short retention, 3) lock project access. If staging uses prod data we need privacy sign-off. See: https://redwood.internal/policies/data-classification
nina: Understood. We're using prod-like traces in staging for 48h only, no mapping stored. Example tag snippet in code: ```tags: { email_hash: sha256(email), tier: customer.tier }```
aj: Also: make sure the Sentry project is restricted (team-only) and retention configured. We have a convention: set SENTRY_RESTRICTED=true and RETENTION_DAYS=7 for staging.
liam: Can you add those details to the PR description (purpose + retention + no-mapping note)? If staging will receive real emails we may need a quick security review, but we can usually sign off fast if the controls are in place.
sarah: One more thing — avoid including domain fragments or tier labels that could be combined to re-identify a user. Keep tags coarse. If you need finer telemetry, file a privacy request.
ops-bot: Reminder: projects sending sensitive identifiers should enable 'pii_masking' in Sentry and follow the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/sentry-pii :warning:
nina: Thanks everyone — I'll add the PR note, set pii_masking and RETENTION_DAYS=7 for staging, and ping here once it's up. :thumbsup:
